answer: Nadir-bound identity anchoring Each agent must register a unique physical sensor reading from a low-noise environmental baseline—such as ambient radio frequency noise at a fixed location—to establish its identity. The system records the nadir (lowest recorded) variance over a rolling epoch; any deviation beyond a calibrated delta triggers revocation. An attacker cannot forge this signal without replicating the exact electromagnetic environment, which requires occupying the same physical space with identical hardware and interference patterns.
